minutes.headline: Select Board unanimously approved the new town manager's contract, starting February 4, 2025; interim manager said farewell.
minutes.summary: Two residents raised complaints about town handling of a certificate of compliance and public records requests. The interim town manager gave his last report, including early FY26 revenue context, and the board voted unanimously to approve the incoming town manager's contract. The board thanked the departing interim manager.

public_comment.topic: Resident said the Conservation Commission delayed and then denied a certificate of compliance beyond the 21-day bylaw deadline and without a written denial.
Resident raised an HOA special permit violation, public records requests, police reports he says were false, Facebook comments about his family, and past tax changes.
Thanked the interim manager and the snow riders, and asked for a response to questions he left with the board.
Further comments on public records compliance, the Secretary of State's involvement, and a volunteer application to the Finance Committee.

votes.motion: Approve the contract of the new town manager, term to begin February 4, 2025.

budget_items.what_was_said: Budget meetings began a modest reorganization of line items as finance reviews the chart of accounts. DPW, facilities and utilities are preparing budget scenarios.
The recommended budget would modestly reorganize staffing and offer more meals a week to seniors.
figures_as_heard: four and maybe five meals a week

budget_items.what_was_said: The state submitted directives to complete before the next revaluation, so funding may be needed to start in FY26.
Funding is coming to the town but it offsets reductions in other areas.
Estimates include the Governor's House 1; new money anticipated gives the town side a share against a retirement assessment increase.
Starting pay, a raise on July 1 and another the following year, slightly under the advertised figure; bonus pay possible via evaluation.
DPW roof and garage floor complete; town hall roof, Ritter roof, library teen room and Council on Aging kitchen progressing; FY21 capital program to close out.

decisions.decision: Board agreed action items will be tracked and reported more regularly, and the agenda-setting process may be discussed on a future agenda.
Meetings set for February 4 and February 11; whether to skip February 11 to be decided next week.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to approve the incoming town manager's contract, with a term beginning February 4, 2025.
The interim town manager gave a last report that included FY26 revenue estimates, the revaluation directives from the state, and budget scenarios in preparation.
The board agreed action items will be tracked and reported more regularly, and that how agendas are set may be discussed at a future meeting.

Two residents complained during public comment about the Conservation Commission's handling of a certificate of compliance and about public records requests; no action was taken on the records complaints.
Meetings are set for February 4 and February 11; the board will decide next week whether to skip the February 11 meeting.

why_it_matters: The town manager's contract sets compensation, including raises and possible bonus pay through evaluation, that will be paid from future town budgets.

The state's revaluation directives may require funding to start in FY26, and the revenue estimates that depend on the Governor's proposal could affect what the town side has available at the budget vote.
